title: Verifier-Guided Repair for LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, full execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostics for the repaired pair, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). For operational use, generated artifacts must satisfy deterministic invariants (required ordering of multi-device commands, field-level constraints, group-level availability constraints, and other policy-level invariants) before deployment. Prototype systems, benchmarks, and tool-augmented agent designs motivate verifier-aware pipelines, but there is limited evidence about the marginal value of a verifier-triggered, bounded repair when the identical initial sample is deterministically reused across comparison conditions.

We conducted a preregistered paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) to estimate exactly that marginal, repair-only effect. Under the preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate contract, each task produced exactly one sampled initial candidate; that same candidate was deterministically reused by both baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator may trigger ≤1 repair) episodes. Consequently, any paired difference can only originate from deterministic validation and the single permitted repair; it cannot arise from independent guarded first-pass generations, selection among multiple samples, or different prompting. The primary estimand is the paired difference in per-task binary acceptance by a deterministic verifier (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Our design therefore isolates repair effects only and does not evaluate other guarded variants (e.g., multi-sample selection, constrained prompts) that were not executed.
sections.related_work:
The supplied verified literature documents active prototyping and benchmarks for intent→configuration workflows and argues for verifier-integrated designs. NetConfEval and related intent→configuration prototypes show feasibility translating natural-language intent to device configurations and benchmark-style evaluations [1]. Deterministic configuration verification methods provide operational oracles for syntactic and semantic invariants (reachability, required sequencing, group-level availability) and form the natural verifier used in our evaluation [2].

Adjacent-domain demonstrations of generate→validate→repair (for example, program-repair pipelines that apply failing-test→patch→regression-test loops) illustrate the architectural pattern and motivate guarded pipelines for correctness, but those demonstrations are primarily in software-engineering tasks and do not by themselves establish repair effectiveness for NetOps where multi-device sequencing and group invariants are salient [4]. Work on tool-augmented agent architectures further motivates coupling generators to specialized solvers and verifiers but emphasizes careful oracle specification and artifacted evaluation [6]. Reporting and preregistration guidance for LLM studies guided our preregistration and archival practices [3].

Synthesis. The verified literature supports (i) active prototype work on intent→config pipelines [1]; (ii) deterministic verifiers as appropriate operational oracles for many configuration correctness properties [2]; and (iii) promise from generate→validate→repair and tool-augmented agent designs in adjacent domains without directly quantifying repair-only effects in multi-device NetOps settings [4],[6]. Our experiment addresses the narrower, underexplored empirical gap of measuring the marginal repair effect when identical initial candidates are reused across baseline and guarded conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design choices. The study design and analysis plan were preregistered (CAND-2026-001) before any model calls. Key predeclared features: paired binary estimand (baseline vs guarded with ≤1 repair), deterministic task selection N=200, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both episodes), a maximum of one automated repair call per task, primary failed-call treatment complete_pair_primary, and the confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar via exact binomial tail) plus a paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistration also fixed the deterministic task generator and verifier implementations used in execution.

Why a paired shared_initial_candidate design? Paired designs reduce between-task variance by comparing the same initial candidate under two post-generation treatments. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the comparison isolates only the downstream validator-triggered repair as an active intervention: because the initial sample is identical for baseline and guarded episodes, prompt reweighting, multiple-sample selection, or independent guarded first-pass generation cannot explain any observed paired differences. This narrower estimand trades broader operational generality for precise identification of repair-only effects.

Task generation and verifier oracle. Tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and selected by the fixed index rule documented in the preregistration. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies. The deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses generated commands, enforces allowed_fields, checks required_sequence ordering, evaluates group-level invariants (final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups), and returns full_intent_constraint_validation=true only when all encoded constraints are satisfied. The verifier emits structured tracer outputs that are authoritative for per-episode scoring; those tracer outputs are archived and were the basis for the confirmatory scoring reported below.

Generation, sanitizer, and repair policy. For each task we executed a deterministic formatting sanitizer before verifier parsing. If the verifier reported invariant violations, the guarded logic could invoke at most one automated repair call to the hosted model with a repair prompt constructed from the validator trace (as preregistered). Repair calls counted against the maximum_model_calls. The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation record exactly one repair call across the run. The model-configuration record declares the requested model as gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset); we explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The experiment used a single initial sample per pair by contract, but nondeterministic hosted-model sampling remains a background property of hosted services and is not ruled out by the recorded configuration.

Statistical analysis. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar test computed from discordant pair counts n10 and n01 using the exact binomial-tail convention (p = 2 × min{BinomCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 − BinomCDF(k − 1; n, 0.5)} with n = n10 + n01 and k = n10). For uncertainty we computed a paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI for the absolute risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The analysis executor and bootstrap parameters are archived and reproduce the reported results.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary counts. The execution manifest records start/end timestamps (UTC) with run elapsed ≈29 minutes. Planned_episode_count = 400 and completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call accounting records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}; cache_miss_count = 201 and cache_hit_count = 0 confirm fresh generations for all shared-initial calls and one repair call.

Confirmatory outcomes. Per the deterministic verifier, baseline successes = 199 and failures = 1 (baseline success_rate = 0.995) and guarded successes = 200 and failures = 0 (guarded success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0, giving paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. With n = n10 + n01 = 1 and k = n10 = 1 the exact two-sided McNemar p-value (exact-binomial convention) equals p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.00, 0.015]. These numeric artifacts are archived and reproduce when the archived analysis executor is re-run on the raw results.

Discordant-pair structure and interpretation. The realized data lie in a sparse-discordant regime (only a single discordant pair). In such regimes the exact McNemar two-sided p-value provides little directional evidence; by construction the two-sided exact binomial-tail yields p = 1.0 when n = 1 and either k = 0 or k = 1 under the conventional handling. The paired-bootstrap CI quantifies plausible magnitudes consistent with the data and bounds the absolute improvement attributable to repair in this repair-only estimand to at most 1.5 percentage points at the 95% percentile level. In short, the experiment rules out moderate-to-large repair-only improvements under these conditions but is underpowered to definitively detect very small absolute gains because of the unexpectedly high baseline pass rate.

Single repair event and failure diagnostic. Exactly one guarded repair was invoked. Archived validator traces for the repaired pair indicate a required_sequence ordering violation prior to repair: the initial candidate breached the task’s required multi-step ordering constraint and the bounded repair produced a reordered command sequence accepted by the deterministic verifier (validation_after.valid = true). The archived per-episode tracer fields record difficulty metadata for the repaired pair (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3, difficulty.level = "extreme"), and the scorer returned score = 1 with scorer_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION" after repair. These tracer fields are the archived evidence that the single observed paired improvement resulted from a verifier-triggered, bounded repair that enacted the required reordering rather than from any alternative sampling or prompt-change effect.

Difficulty-stratified diagnostics. Representative task manifests and validator traces encode difficulty features used in exploratory interpretation (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). In the archived representative subset required_command_count spans 3–9 and changed_interface_count values up to 3; the lone baseline failure and the repaired pair both appear associated with the higher end of these difficulty measures. This pattern is consistent with the preregistered exploratory hypothesis that multi-device sequencing and higher required_command_count concentrate residual failures that bounded repair can sometimes fix when violations are expressible in the verifier’s manifest-coded invariants.
sections.discussion:
What the repair-only estimand measures. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the comparison isolates post-generation validator logic and the single permitted repair as the only difference between episodes. Therefore, the observed paired outcome difference is interpretable strictly as a repair-only effect on the same initial candidate; it does not measure benefits that would accrue from re-sampling, guarded constrained prompts, or multi-candidate selection. Any operational claims about those other interventions would require separate executed comparisons.

Interpreting small observed improvement and the statistical regime. The realized baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) substantially exceeded the mid-range baseline assumptions used in power planning (45–65%), placing the confirmatory test in a sparse-discordant regime and reducing sensitivity to small absolute improvements. With only one discordant pair the exact two-sided McNemar p-value gives limited directional evidence (p = 1.0), while the paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] bounds the plausible repair-only absolute effect sizes compatible with the data. Thus, while the guarded pipeline produced one concrete repair-mediated correction, the dataset is consistent with at most small absolute improvements under our repair-only estimand; moderate or large repair-only gains are ruled out by these results in this synthetic verifier-backed setting.

What the single repaired case implies. The archived tracer evidence shows a concrete mechanism by which a bounded, verifier-triggered repair corrected a multi-step ordering violation expressible in the task's required_sequence. This supports a constrained operational conclusion: when violations are expressible in a deterministic verifier’s manifest (ordering and workflow policies encoded in required_sequence and workflow_policies), a bounded repair that uses validator traces to construct a targeted repair prompt can sometimes convert an invalid configuration into a valid one. The repaired case had extreme composite difficulty (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3), suggesting that complex multi-step sequencing errors are an important failure mode that repair logic can address in at least some instances.

Limitations and threats to validity. Internal validity: the paired shared_initial_candidate design isolates repair effects but does not address prompt sensitivity, model sampling variability, or alternative guarded semantics that generate independent first-pass candidates. Crucially, the recorded model configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a rich set of manifest-encoded invariants but is not a substitute for dataplane emulation or vendor-specific runtime semantics. External validity: the run used a synthetic deterministic task bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini); findings therefore do not demonstrate multi-model generality or live-device deployment safety. Adversarial/contamination threats: the run did not include adversarial poisoning or retrieval-contamination experiments. Statistical: with only one discordant pair the power to detect small repair-only effects is limited; the paired-bootstrap CI quantifies this uncertainty.

Operational implications and future work. Artifact-grounded evidence justifies a narrow operational message: verifier-guided bounded repair can remediate certain ordering/dependency violations in generated configurations when those violations are captured by the verifier’s manifest. Evaluating whether bounded repair reduces operator triage time, improves deployment safety, or scales across models and production topologies requires follow-up experiments that execute independent-first-pass guarded semantics, include multiple LLMs, and integrate dataplane emulation or live-device execution. Adversarial contamination and RAG/retrieval-based contamination effects also remain open empirical axes.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In 200 synthetic deterministic tasks with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. Paired absolute risk difference = 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. Artifact-grounded evidence therefore supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded bounded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic verifier-backed setting. Broader operational claims require additional experiments (multi-model studies, independent-first-pass guarded semantics, adversarial contamination testing, live-device/dataplane emulation).

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier (oracle): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Archived provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are available in the execution bundle for audit.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
